text:
alex.k: Heads up — since ~10:02 us-west GPU nodes intermittently fail resolving our internal model registry `models-internal.svc.cluster.local`. Pods that pull images hang during provisioning, onboarding GPUs into the fleet is stuck for some batches.

maria.l: seeing the same from node-ukr-02. kubelet logs show `getaddrinfo: Name or service not known` when talking to the registry IP.

sasha: quick check — is this only within the cluster DNS or split-horizon / egress impacted?

alex.k: looks split-horizon: from bastion we can resolve the public name, but pods resolve to internal cluster name and sometimes it returns NXDOMAIN. Noticed `ndots` in `/etc/resolv.conf` on nodes is `ndots:1`.

ben: ndots=1 will try short names first; with our search domains ordering it can hit external resolvers incorrectly. paste of node resolv.conf:
```
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local company.internal
nameserver 169.254.20.10  # node-local-dns
nameserver 10.0.0.2        # NAT'ed egress resolver
options ndots:1 timeout:2 attempts:2
```

maria.l: aha — node-local-dns should answer cluster.local, but I've seen it forward to egress when cache misses happen. TTLs for some SRV records are low (5s) so racey.

sasha: can you `dig` from a pod and from the host?

alex.k: from pod (busybox):
```
$ dig +short models-internal.svc.cluster.local @169.254.20.10
# sometimes empty
```
from node: `dig +short models-internal.svc.cluster.local @169.254.20.10` returns IP intermittently.

infra-bot: Rolling alert -> DNS error rate spiked 4x on us-west.

ben: possibility: iptables rule for node-local cache got bypassed after a kernel upgrade, traffic went directly to egress NAT and hit our split-horizon egress resolver which returns NXDOMAIN for cluster names.

maria.l: confirmed — `iptables -t nat -L` on node-ukr-02 shows the TPROXY redirect to 169.254.20.10 missing for udp/53.

alex.k: mitigation plan: 1) add temporary kubelet `resolvConf` override to point pods to `169.254.20.10` explicitly; 2) adjust `ndots:5` in node resolv.conf via cloud-init for new nodes; 3) restart node-local-dns DaemonSet after ensuring iptables rules are reapplied.

sasha: for immediate unblock, set `resolver` env on the model-registry deployment to the FQDN IP so image pulls use full name and skip search. small patch: `imagePullSecrets` won't help dns.

ben: rolling a quick DaemonSet restart now (canary on 2 nodes) and adding an iptables rule to restore 53->169.254.20.10. watching provisioner.

alex.k: also seeing a few cases where `systemd-resolved` on the host left a stub at `127.0.0.53` before node-local-dns got bound; resolv.conf ordering changed after node restart. we should standardize: node-local-dns first, then systemd stub, then egress.

maria.l: agree. long-term: add e2e test for resolv.conf ordering and ndots behavior in cluster upgrade pipeline. ticket #OPS-1123.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary restart completed 2/2 nodes, no regression posted.

sasha: status update?

ben: after fix: DNS errors dropped back to baseline, provisioning resumed, +30 GPU nodes joined the pool in the last 10m. added cloud-init change to image for new node rollouts to set `ndots:5` and to ensure `ip` rule for node-local-dns is persisted.

alex.k: follow-ups: 1) postmortem note about kernel upgrade interactions with iptables persistence; 2) add a resolv.conf lint in node bootstrap; 3) consider making node-local-dns use a non-privileged port with iptables restoration controlled by daemonset.

maria.l: will open the postmortem and the bootstrap PR. thanks for the quick patching. :thumbsup:

sasha: nice catch on ndots. leaving notes in runbook about split-horizon tests.

alex.k: closing thread once PRs are up and new nodes in staging validate.
